'''YTL Communications Sdn. Bhd.''' [[doing business as|''dba'']] '''Yes''' is a [[mobile network operator]] in [[Malaysia]], the fifth in the country overall. Headquartered in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, YTL Communications is a subsidiary of the utilities company [[YTL Power|YTL Power International Berhad]] and serves as the communications arm of [[YTL Corporation|YTL Corporation Berhad]], an infrastructure conglomerate in Malaysia. Yes uses the native dialling prefix identifier of 018 and 011-1.

== Network and coverage ==

=== 4G LTE ===
Yes 4G operates [[LTE (telecommunication)|4G LTE]] and [[LTE Advanced|4G LTE-A]] networks.

The Yes network is built from the ground up with an all-IP architecture, making it the first and only all-4G and all-IP network provider in Malaysia capable of offering unique services such as user ID-based unified communications as well as session concurrency for mobile data and telephony services.

Yes owns and operates its own network infrastructure in Malaysia. Yes has close to 5,000 base stations across the country with an all-4G network footprint reaching over 85% population coverage nationwide.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.soyacincau.com/2016/06/15/yes-rolls-out-lte-widest-4g-coverage-with-volte-support/|title=Yes rolls out LTE. Widest 4G coverage with VoLTE support|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>

[[WiMAX]] networks were discontinued on 1 October 2019.<ref name="Yes 4G WiMAX shutdown">{{cite web |title=Yes says goodbye to WiMAX |url=https://soyacincau.com/2019/10/01/yes-says-goodbye-to-wimax/ |website=soyacincau |access-date=1 October 2019}}</ref>

It is also the first in Malaysia to provide nationwide [[Voice over LTE|VoLTE]] (Voice over LTE), available for [[Android (operating system)|Android]] VoLTE-supported smartphones.

=== 5G ===
<!-- Please add frequencies and network stabilities to this part if you can -->

In December 2021, Yes is one of the first operators (along with unifi Mobile) to roll out 5G pilot test for consumers in Malaysia, branded as ''Yes FT5G''.<ref>{{Cite web|title=First 5G in Malaysia|url=https://www.yes.my/5gplans/|access-date=2022-02-21|website=Yes {{!}} First to 5G|language=en-US}}</ref> The backbone of Yes's 5G service is powered by [[Digital Nasional Berhad]],<ref>{{Cite web|last=Zahiid|first=Syed Jaymal|title=DNB rolls out 5G test pilot through YES and Unifi Mobile {{!}} Malay Mail|url=https://www.malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2021/12/15/dnb-rolls-out-5g-test-pilot-through-yes-and-unifi-mobile/2028557|access-date=2022-02-21|website=www.malaymail.com|language=en}}</ref> and it's currently available in Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and Cyberjaya.

In May 26 2022, Yes launched the Infinite plans, bringing Malaysia to the world map for providing the most economical data usage plans. The event was graced by the MCMC Minister, [[Malay styles and titles#Tan Sri|Tan Sri]] [[Malay styles and titles#State titles|Datuk Seri Panglima]] [[Hajji|Haji]] [[Annuar Musa]] at Majestic Hotel Kuala Lumpur. Major device manufacturers (Samsung, Xiaomi, Oppo and Vivo) are also backing Yes in collaboration to sell Yes Infinite+ plans with their devices. Yes Infinite plans have no tonnage capping, no speed capping and no bill shocks, the only capping is on the plan monthly fee. A free 5G device is included if subscribers opt for the contract.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Coverage|url=https://www.yes.my/coverage/|access-date=2022-02-21|website=Yes {{!}} First to 5G|language=en-US}}</ref>

== Services to the education sector ==
Yes has worked closely with the Malaysian [[Ministry of Education (Malaysia)|Ministry of Education]] to equip all 10,000 primary and secondary national schools across the country with high-speed 4G Internet connectivity integrated with cloud-based Frog<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://frogasia.com/en/frog-vle/|title=Frog VLE|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210116130336/https://frogasia.com/en/frog-vle/|archive-date=16 January 2021|access-date=|url-status=dead}}</ref> [[Virtual learning environment|VLE]] (Virtual Learning Environment) platform under the [http://btp.moe.gov.my/1bestarinet 1BestariNet] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180418065124/http://btp.moe.gov.my/1bestarinet |date=18 April 2018 }} program.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.yes.my/what-we-do#onebestarinet|title=1BestariNet|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>

Under Yes' own Education Partner Programme (EPP), it entered into strategic partnerships with selected public colleges and universities within Malaysia to furnish the entire campus grounds and buildings with high-speed 4G Internet connectivity and free data to access the Internet for educational purposes.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.yes.my/media-centre/20100701|title=Creating Malaysia's First 4G Campus-wide Network|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160908222058/http://www.yes.my/media-centre/20100701|archive-date=8 September 2016|access-date=|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== History ==
Yes was officially launched on 19 November 2010 in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.thesundaily.my/node/136046|title=YTL launches converged 4G network|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.soyacincau.com/2010/11/03/ytl-comms-reveals-4g-service-brand-yes/|title=YTL Comms reveals 4G service brand – YES|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref> and was the first in the world to commercially launch a converged 4G network at a national scale based on IEEE Broadband Wireless Access Standards (WiMAX). At launch, it boasted 65% nationwide population coverage and was the largest 4G network in Malaysia.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.computerworld.com.my/tech/emerging-technology/malaysias-yes-4g-is-one-of-the-most-advanced-in-the-world-idc/|title=Malaysia's Yes 4G is one of the most advanced in the world: IDC|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180620002413/https://www.computerworld.com.my/tech/emerging-technology/malaysias-yes-4g-is-one-of-the-most-advanced-in-the-world-idc/|archive-date=20 June 2018|access-date=|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Yes first started out with a prepaid service, charging 9 sen for 3MB of data, or an SMS or a minute of voice call which was compatible with its 4G devices namely Yes Go USB dongle and Yes Huddle mobile hotspot device. A postpaid version of the Yes plan service called Super Postpaid Plan was launched in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.hardwarezone.com.my/tech-news-yes-unveils-unlimited-super-postpaid-plans|title=Yes unveils unlimited Super postpaid plans|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180619193056/http://www.hardwarezone.com.my/tech-news-yes-unveils-unlimited-super-postpaid-plans|archive-date=19 June 2018|access-date=|url-status=dead}}</ref> Yes also introduced several 4G smartphones, including Yes Buzz,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.soyacincau.com/2011/03/04/yes-buzz-yes-zoom-now-available/|title=Yes Buzz & Yes Zoom now available|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref> Yes Altitude and Yes Eclipse.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mobile88.com/cellphone/yes/yes-eclipse-4g/specification.asp|title=Yes Eclipse|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180619163411/http://www.mobile88.com/cellphone/yes/yes-eclipse-4g/specification.asp|archive-date=19 June 2018|access-date=|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Awarded with 80&nbsp;MHz of the 4G spectrum, Yes officially launched its 4G LTE services including VoLTE on 30 June 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thestar.com.my/tech/tech-news/2016/06/30/yes-officially-launches-4g-lte-network/|title=Yes rolls out 4G LTE service with VoLTE|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nst.com.my/news/2016/06/155836/yes-unveils-new-double-data-4g-lte-plans-4g-volte-smartphone|title=YES unveils new 'Double Data' 4G LTE plans, 4G VoLTE smartphone|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>

Yes announced in January 2018 that its nationwide network fully supports [[4G+]] or LTE-Advanced.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thestar.com.my/tech/tech-news/2018/01/10/4g-connectivity-is-available-in-malaysia/|title=4G+ connectivity is available in Malaysia|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>
